name: Input
purpose: Single-line text entry with label, description and error wired to ARIA.
notFor: Controls with their own keyboard model — date pickers, comboboxes

hideLabel.note: Hides visually, keeps it for assistive tech. Kept in React for the one legitimate case - a search field whose surrounding context already names it - and deliberately not carried into Angular, because in practice it is used to remove labels from ERP toolbars and the placeholder is then expected to do the job. A placeholder disappears on focus and is not a voice-control target (WCAG 2.5.3). Angular's Input.stories.ts documents the refusal under the same story name.

description.note: A string, not a slot. It is referenced by aria-describedby, which needs a stable id on a single element — a projected node the consumer controls can be a fragment, several elements, or none, and none of those can be pointed at. Select and Checkbox agree.

error.note: Its presence is what sets aria-invalid.

keyboard.Tab: Moves focus to the input. Native.

aria.labelling: From the associated <label>, required. A placeholder is not a name: it disappears on focus and is not a voice-control target.
aria.focus: Ring on the input itself. Never removed on :focus-visible.
aria.announcements: None. The error is in aria-describedby, read on focus. Announcing a validation error as it appears interrupts typing, which is when it usually appears.

attributes.aria-describedby: error id then description id, in that order
